text:
maria: Heads up — token-level breakdown shows a sudden tail-latency spike for /v1/generate (fast-kernel pool) around 02:10 UTC. 95th/99th jumped ~3x. KV cache hit-rate fell from ~96% -> ~70% in same window. Any recent kernel selection rollouts or cache changes?

sam: I deployed a kernel-selector tweak last night to prefer fused_attn_v2 on Ampere for seq_len>512. It was staged but may have overlapped with canary routing. I can roll it back quickly.

devon: I grabbed a quick profiler snippet — putting the relevant logs inline:

```
[02:09:58] model-serving: chosen_kernel=fused_attn_v2 reason=auto
[02:09:58] batch_size=1 seq_len=1024 kv_hit=false
[02:10:04] token_latency_ms=18 tail_95_ms=820 tail_99_ms=1200
[02:10:10] routing: shard=fast-kernel-3 queue_len=0
```

julia-sre: Pager rules triggered (latency burn-rate) at ~02:12 for us-east-1; our paging threshold is set to burn_rate>0.7 over 5m, we were at 0.85. But the alert didn't page because the rule requires both burn_rate and route_error_ratio>0.01. I think the error ratio was low so we didn't page. We should discuss whether paging should be allowed on burn-rate alone for token-level SLO degradations.

sam: Reverting selector now (rolling back canary). Also, batching heuristics were adjusted in the same deploy to prefer micro-batches when concurrency < 3 — that could increase per-token latency for long sequences. I'll flip the batching flag after rollback to isolate.

maria: Action items: (1) @sam revert kernel-selector (in flight) (2) @devon investigate KV cache eviction + redis TTLs around 01:30-02:10 (3) @julia-sre propose temporary paging rule change to include burn-rate-only on per-route token-latency SLOs. If page fires, runbook: follow the latency checklist and scale dedicated pool.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollback initiated by @sam — rollout id r-2026-03-18-0715, progress 40%

sam: Rollback completed at 02:18. Fast-kernel nodes are back to previous kernel_selector. Monitoring: 95th latency trending down but KV miss rate still elevated.

devon: Dug into redis cluster TTLs — found a maintenance script changed model-cache TTL from 24h -> 30m at 01:25 (oops). Reverted to 24h at 02:22. KV hit-rate back to ~94% after warm-up. Looks like the dominant cause for KV misses was the TTL churn, not kernel itself.

julia-sre: I'll open a PR to change the paging rule: add a contingency for token-latency-burn-rate > 0.6 for 5m to page on-call, scoped per-route. Also adding an anomaly detector that uses median+MAD baseline (short window) to avoid noisy pages for heavy-tail workloads. Assigning to @maria for review.

maria: Thanks. Two follow-ups: (A) add token-level histogram buckets (1ms steps up to 50ms, then 50-200ms linear, then log) to the per-route dashboard so the SRE runbook can inspect distribution quickly, (B) add an automated check that correlates kernel-selection rollouts with KV hit-rate deltas before promoting to 100%.

sam: +1 on both. I'll add the rollout-gate check to the experiment pipeline.

maria: Nice work — closing the incident for now. If anyone sees a reoccurrence, ping #eng-runtime and page per the new rule. :thumbsup:
